issues.problem: The loop now calls FileUtils.delete(String) for every component and ignores its boolean return. Before the patch, every component except SUMMARY went through FileUtils.deleteWithConfirm, which threw FSWriteError on failure. That error went to the disk failure policy and was logged with the cause. FileUtils.delete(String) is File.delete(). It returns false on failure, with no exception, no log and no metric. A DATA, INDEX or other component that fails to delete (permissions, I/O error, a busy file) now fails silently, and SSTable.delete() still returns true. The SSTable is left partially deleted. This is the same leaked-file and partial-delete state the ticket is trying to fix, and an operator would see no sign of it. It also disables the disk failure policy for these paths. The only message left is the 'Deleting sstable' info line, logged before any deletion happens.
issues.fix: Keep deleteWithConfirm for all components in the sorted loop, so FSWriteError and the failure policy still apply. If SUMMARY needs the old lenient treatment, keep it lenient but log a warn with the file path when delete() returns false. Do not discard the return value.

also_fixes.fix: Use FileUtils.deleteWithConfirm for all components, as before. Keep the old best-effort FileUtils.delete behaviour only for SUMMARY, and then only if the sort order still allows it.
Keep the sorted order but use FileUtils.deleteWithConfirm(desc.filenameFor(component)) for every component except SUMMARY. Keep SUMMARY on the non-throwing FileUtils.delete.

lenses.name: cassandra-standards
lenses.summary: The patch changes SSTable.delete() in src/java/org/apache/cassandra/io/sstable/SSTable.java. It now reads each component's lastModified once, sorts the components by that value, and deletes them oldest first. The aim is to keep the SSTable's most-recent timestamp stable across a partial delete, so LogFile.verifyRecord() does not fail after a crash. This matches the core of CASSANDRA-21649. However, the patch also replaces FileUtils.deleteWithConfirm with FileUtils.delete for every component. The old code used deleteWithConfirm for everything except SUMMARY. The new FileUtils.delete(String) returns a boolean that is now ignored, so a failed delete no longer throws FSWriteError or reaches the JVMStabilityInspector path. The ticket's test plan calls for additions to LogTransactionTest, and the diff contains no test. This is a 4.0 backport, which is appropriate for a bug fix, and the change is small. Minor risks are the lack of a tie-breaker for equal timestamps and a missing-file lastModified of 0 that sorts first.

lenses.name: correctness
lenses.summary: SSTable.delete() now sorts components by lastModified and deletes oldest-first, which fixes the ordering bug in the ticket. One regression: it replaced FileUtils.deleteWithConfirm with FileUtils.delete for every component, so failed deletions are now silent. Imports compile (java.io.* and java.util.* are already imported). I did not review the tests: the diff contains none, although the ticket's test plan names LogTransactionTest additions.

findings.problem: The old code called FileUtils.deleteWithConfirm for every component except SUMMARY. That call throws FSWriteError when a delete fails, for example on a permissions problem. The new loop calls FileUtils.delete(String) for all components. That method only calls File.delete() and returns false on failure, and the return value is ignored. A failed delete of the DATA, INDEX or other component is now silent, and SSTable.delete() still returns true. The caller then treats the SSTable as removed, so files leak with no error. A leftover file can also cause the same REMOVE-record mismatch on restart that this patch is meant to prevent. Only SUMMARY was previously best-effort.
findings.fix: Keep the sorted order but use FileUtils.deleteWithConfirm(desc.filenameFor(component)) for every component except SUMMARY. Keep SUMMARY on the non-throwing FileUtils.delete.

findings.problem: lastModified is read with File.lastModified() once per component, and that call returns 0 for a missing file. A component that is already absent sorts first, which is harmless. Components with equal timestamps are ordered by the Set's iteration order. That is still safe, because the maximum timestamp is only lost once every file sharing it has been deleted. The ordering therefore relies on coarse filesystem timestamp granularity and is not deterministic. No test covers it.
findings.fix: Add a tiebreaker such as the component name to make the order deterministic. Add a LogTransactionTest case that partially deletes an SSTable and checks that the REMOVE record still verifies.
